title: Project Plan
description: The project plan most junior PMs over-build and then never look at again. A working plan is one page of dates and dependencies, three views of the same truth, designed to survive contact with reality. The Gantt chart is the artefact; the dependencies are the document.

# Customer Portal Programme — Project Plan
_v0.4 · 22 April 2026 · Adekunle Bello_

## 1. One-paragraph framing

Replace the legacy customer portal with a self-service experience for the top 12,000 B2B customers. Go-live target: 9 September 2026. Delivers account management, three report types, self-service password reset, and an admin console for our customer-success team.

## 2. Phases + milestones

| Phase | Starts | Ends | Milestone |
|-------|--------|------|-----------|
| Discovery | 1 May | 22 May | Signed BRD + architecture decision record |
| Build wave 1 | 23 May | 4 July | Account mgmt + login features deployable to staging |
| Build wave 2 | 5 July | 15 Aug | Reports + admin console deployable to staging |
| UAT | 18 Aug | 5 Sep | UAT sign-off from CS + finance |
| Go-live | 8 Sep | 9 Sep | Cutover Mon evening, live Tue 9 Sep |

## 3. Dependencies

| Dependency | Owner | Needed by | Status |
|------------|-------|-----------|--------|
| SSO config from IT | Tomasz Wójcik (IT) | 14 June | Open — meeting booked 6 May |
| Customer data pipeline (data platform team) | Rohan Chatterjee | 28 June | At risk — see RAID R-04 |
| Compliance sign-off on data residency | Marcus Klein | 8 August | Not started — will book in week 7 |
| Vendor contract renewal (Synth Logistics) | Procurement | 1 July | Closed |

## 4. Resource shape

| Role | FTE on this | Names | Window |
|------|-------------|-------|--------|
| Eng (FE) | 2.0 | Lewis Harding, Theo Park | May–Sep |
| Eng (BE) | 2.0 | Asha Bhatt, contractor TBC | May–Sep |
| QA | 1.0 | Naledi Mokoena | Jun–Sep |
| Designer | 0.5 | Theo Park (split) | May–Aug |
| BA | 1.0 | (TBC — covering with myself for now) | May–Aug |

## 5. Critical path

1. Discovery → BRD sign-off (4 days float)
2. SSO config land in build wave 1 (0 days float — this is the constraint)
3. Customer data pipeline land before UAT (5 days float — see R-04)
4. Compliance data residency sign-off before cutover (3 days float)
5. UAT sign-off before cutover (1 day float)

## 6. RAID summary

Full register at /raid/customer-portal. Top three:

- **R-04 (high):** Customer data pipeline at risk; depends on cross-team commitment from data platform group. Mitigation: weekly check-in with Rohan, escalation to Programme Director if not on track by 1 June.
- **R-07 (med):** SSO config team has one engineer on holiday weeks 5–6. Mitigation: confirmed the work is in-flight before holiday.
- **R-11 (med):** Compliance has signalled a data residency question. Mitigation: book the conversation in week 7, don't let it surface in UAT.

## 7. Assumptions

1. The customer data pipeline (data platform team) delivers in scope by 28 June. If late, build wave 2 compresses or slips.
2. We do not migrate historical customer data in this programme. Phase 2 candidate. If business pushes for it, end date moves to November.
3. Compliance accepts UK + EU data residency (current model). If they require UK-only, architecture changes and the date slips a month.

annotations.note: One paragraph. Three sentences. If you can't frame the programme in three sentences, you don't yet understand it. The framing-paragraph test is the cheapest sanity check on whether you actually own the work.

Dependencies is the section most rookie PMs treat as 'and then we'll do this'. Reality: 80% of programme slippage is dependency slippage. Each dependency needs a named owner and a needed-by date. Status field at four values: Closed / On track / Open / At risk. Anything else is mush.
Critical path is the four-to-six tasks where you do not have float. If your critical path is twenty tasks long, you don't have one — you have a wish list. The discipline is in the cut.

Assumptions are the section senior reviewers read first. Each assumption is a sentence whose negation changes the plan materially. 'We assume we will deliver on time' is not an assumption; it's a fortune cookie.

common_mistakes: Full task lists in the Gantt — every story, every standup. The plan becomes unmaintained within a month and stops being trusted. The Gantt is for phases and milestones. The story-level work lives in the sprint tooling.
Dependencies section omitted, or buried in the RAID register. Dependencies are the document. If they're not at the top, they will be missed.
Critical path of fifteen tasks. That's not a critical path; that's a fear of cutting. Six tasks max.
Assumptions written defensively ('we assume the team will perform'). Assumptions exist to be negated; write them precisely enough that a stakeholder can challenge them.
No owner column on dependencies. 'IT' is not an owner. A named person is.

Resource shape with FTE counts that don't add up to a real headcount available — the plan looks beautiful and the team can't execute it. Always sanity-check against actual capacity, including the half-day-a-week your QA spends supporting other programmes.
variant_patterns: Regulatory programme variant: add §8 'Regulatory milestones' (FCA / GDPR sign-off dates) and §9 'External evidence trail' (what gets logged where for audit). Critical path almost always runs through the regulator's calendar, not yours.
Discovery variant: §2 collapses to 'discovery phases' (problem framing / solution sketch / business case). §5 critical path is replaced by 'decision dates' — when each go/no-go is needed.
Multi-vendor variant: §3 dependencies become the primary section. Vendor contractual SLAs go above named individuals — escalation paths are different.
